results.headline: Death toll tops 470 as barrier lake overflow halts Nepal-Bhutan rescue
results.reason: headline: says the rescue is a 'Nepal-Bhutan' operation, but every cited source (e.g. A2, A13, A6) describes the disaster and rescue as occurring on the Nepal-Tibet/China border; Bhutan is not mentioned in any cited source, and the story's own summary correctly says 'Nepal-Tibet border', contradicting the headline.

results.headline: Norway's King Harald V dies at 89; son Haakon takes throne
results.reason: Matches cited sources: death at 89 on Friday at Oslo University Hospital, automatic succession by Haakon, 35-year reign, Mette-Marit/Epstein correspondence and Høiby's rape conviction all supported by A4/A74.

results.headline: Ratko Mladić, convicted of genocide at Srebrenica, dies in Hague prison
results.reason: summary: states Mladić was convicted of genocide for massacring 'at least 12,000 Muslims' at Srebrenica, but cited sources give the figure as 'at least 8,000' (A115: 'at least 8,000 Muslims'; A225: 'at least 8,000 Muslims'; A358: 'some 8,000 Muslims'). No cited source supports 12,000.

results.headline: US judge rules Pentagon's blacklisting of Anthropic was illegal
results.reason: Matches cited sources: Judge Rita Lin's 59-page order, First Amendment retaliation framing, first-ever public designation under the statute, and the surveillance/autonomous-weapons refusal are all supported by A8/A58.

results.headline: Trump says Putin will not attack NATO as Pentagon prepares European defence options
results.reason: Matches cited sources: A39/A408/A576 support Colby's Brussels remarks, four options by Nov 6 and December deadline; A410's headline confirms Trump downplaying the Ratcliffe trip, and A148 confirms reports the 'CIA chief' warned Moscow, jointly supporting the claim.

results.headline: Iran agrees to draw up Hormuz conditions list; US clears strait of mines
results.reason: why_it_matters: refers to 'a closure the Biden administration has so far failed to reverse,' but every cited source describes the current administration as Trump's (e.g., A31/A34 reference Trump declaring the MOU 'over', Reuters datelined Aug 2026); no cited source mentions a Biden administration currently in office, making this a stale/incorrect world-state assertion.

results.headline: DRC launches Ebola vaccination drive as death toll reaches 2,744
results.reason: why_it_matters: claims 'renewed armed clashes in North Kivu have already forced three vaccination sites to suspend work,' but none of the cited sources (A17, A20, A539, A604, A698) mention North Kivu clashes or any vaccination-site suspensions; A17 places the outbreak in Ituri province, not North Kivu.

results.headline: Syria appoints Kurdish commander Abdi as presidential adviser and allows Kurdish-language schooling
results.reason: Matches cited sources: A36 confirms Abdi's appointment and Kurdish-language schooling decision; A37 confirms Abdi's Interpol red notice and Turkey's wanted list, and Tom Barrack's endorsement of the integration model.

results.headline: Russia strikes Kyiv for second straight day; Kherson told to evacuate
results.reason: Matches cited sources: A221 confirms one death and damage figures (14 warehouses, 16 homes, three apartment blocks); A220 confirms Kherson governor's evacuation call, glide-bomb strike on the heating plant, and 'no way to destroy' the drones/bombs, plus last winter's power-plant strikes.

results.headline: Chinese executives may join Xi's September US visit; trade truce extension seen as near-certain
results.reason: why_it_matters: asserts Washington and Beijing are managing 'a range of active disputes including Iran-related sanctions pressure,' but none of the cited sources (A491, A501, A505) mention Iran or Iran-related sanctions in connection with US-China relations.

results.headline: Bangladesh journalists jailed since 2024 remain detained as BNP fails to honour press-freedom pledge
results.reason: summary: states 'Five journalists and a writer' remain in detention, but cited source A581 names only 'Four Bangladeshi journalists ... and writer Shahriar Kabir' (i.e., four journalists plus one writer, five people total), contradicting the 'five journalists' count.

results.headline: Taiwan parliament passes its own drone plan and backs $7bn boost for domestic builders
results.reason: Matches cited sources: A456 confirms parliament rejected the government drone plan and passed its own; A714 confirms the $7 billion boost for domestic drone builders; A497 supports the why_it_matters claim about typhoons/heat disrupting Taiwan Strait military planning.

results.headline: Australia severs ties with two Chinese universities as Pacific rivalry sharpens
results.reason: Matches cited sources: A495 confirms the university partnership cuts on national security grounds, alignment with US restrictions, and the analyst's warning about Australia being locked out of top-tier research; A292 confirms the Pacific rivalry sharpened after Beijing's ICBM test.

results.headline: Trump chip tariff plan could cost $90bn in annual GDP and delay one-fifth of US data centre projects, industry warns
results.reason: summary: claims the broadest tariff approach would 'delay or cancel most data centre projects planned through 2030,' but cited source A47 states the CCIA estimate is about 20 percent (one-fifth) of such projects — the same figure correctly used in this story's own headline — so 'most' contradicts the sourced 20 percent figure.

results.headline: Fed chair Warsh's Jackson Hole debut scrutinised for rate signals as inflation persists above target
results.reason: summary: names 'Governors Michelle Bowman, Christopher Waller and Lisa Cook' as the three dissenters favouring a rate hike, but the only cited source with content on this (A29) merely says 'three of them dissenting in favour of a hike' without naming them; no cited source identifies the three governors by name.

results.headline: Zambia opposition leader detained on treason charges ahead of president's inauguration
results.reason: summary: claims Mundubile 'finished second to incumbent President Hakainde Hichilema by fewer than 40,000 votes,' but neither cited source (A161, A577) gives a specific vote margin; A161 only states Hichilema won 'around 60% of the vote.'

results.headline: Japan's births rise for first time in 11 years
results.reason: summary: gives specific figures ('731,000 babies born, a 1.8 percent increase') and attributes the cause to 'a post-pandemic rebound in marriages,' but the sole cited source A289's available content is identical to its headline ('Japan's number of births rises for first time in 11 years') with no supporting detail, so none of these specifics can be verified.
